[Tasks native Start on Vite+ and Cloudflare](/build/devops/tasks-viteplus-cloudflare)
describes the runtime and artifact format.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-tasks` |
| Canonical route | `tasks.tuturuuu.com/*`, root mode |
| Assets | `ASSETS` with worker-first routing and `html_handling: none` |
| Runtime public inputs | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` |
| Required secrets | `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`. Optional bindings are listed in `apps/tasks/env.example`. |
| Offline behavior | The native shell does not register the legacy Next.js service worker. |

## Publish from production

The Production Deployment Planner selects `tasks-cloudflare.yaml` for Tasks.
The publisher calls the `tasks-cutover-artifact` producer in
`mail-calendar-tasks-builds.yaml` for the planner's production SHA and downloads
`tasks-cutover-production-<sha>` from the same run. The producer keeps its regular
push, dispatch and PR build paths. The legacy Vercel Tasks publisher is disabled.

Trusted main and production builds require the configured production Supabase
URL and publishable key. Placeholder public inputs belong to fixture builds.

The publish job compares the downloaded archive's SHA-256 with the producer job
output, then verifies the production profile, source SHA and sealed file
hashes. The production-only `tasks-production` environment supplies
`TASKS_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. Use an Individual Workers Editor grant scoped to
`tuturuuu-tasks`.
The `deploy-tasks` caller in `vercel-production.yaml` must keep
`secrets: inherit`; a reusable workflow resolves that environment secret as
empty without forwarded secrets, and the publisher aborts before any write.
The job uses the pinned Wrangler upload adapter for the sealed Void output.
The `cf` upload path can replace it after qualification against the same
Tasks server modules, static assets and existing bindings.

The publisher captures the active deployment and its 100% rollback version,
uploads the sealed output without bundling, and registers the candidate at
0% traffic. A version override runs the smoke on the canonical hostname with
the candidate's assets and verifies the exact SHA. The publisher checks the
production ref again immediately before shifting traffic to the candidate.
The publisher then verifies public build identity and runs the smoke once per
minute for ten minutes. It rolls back when a route check fails or when probes
exceed the greater of 2 seconds and three times baseline latency in consecutive
samples. The sanitized release receipt contains both version IDs and the smoke
results. The explicit `tasks-cloudflare` deployment marker records success only
after verification.

The live edge can return `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` even though the Worker
sets `DENY`. The standalone smoke reports the discrepancy. The publisher
accepts it only on routes where the previous version also returned
`SAMEORIGIN` and the enforcing CSP still returns `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
Review the retained per-route results during release verification.

The publisher accepts only the same-run production artifact
`tasks-cutover-production-<sha>`. Its digest, source ref and production profile
must all match the release.

## Smoke and rollback

```bash
node scripts/native-cutover/smoke.mjs --origin https://tasks.tuturuuu.com --app tasks --expect native
curl --fail --silent --show-error -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' \
  "https://tasks.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info?check=$(date +%s)"
```

Check the full `commitHash`. The smoke covers robots, central login and path
preservation, the signed-out boards API, the server-function guard, crawler
rendering, a built asset and frame protection.

Use the `previousVersion` from the publication receipt for rollback. The
publisher checks that its deployment still owns traffic before restoring that
version. After an interrupted run, reconcile the current Cloudflare deployment
and the receipt before any further write. If the failed release is still active,
restore the prior version to 100% in Cloudflare and confirm the canonical
build-info returns `previousSha`. Keep the Worker route attached.
